problems.title: Enlarging the intervention set can reduce MACE, invalidating the unrestricted nonnegativity theorem
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, Lemma 1 and Theorem 2, PDF p. 5; proof, PDF p. 6; Appendix A.1, Lemma 2, PDF p. 13.
claim: Paraphrase of the complete relevant claims: Appendix A.1, Lemma 2 (p. 13), asserts that \(A\subseteq B\) implies \(m(A)\leq m(B)\). Section 3.2, Lemma 1 (p. 5), asserts monotonicity of \(r\) on the redundancy order. Theorem 2 (p. 5; proof on p. 6) then asserts \(C(\alpha;Y)\geq0\) for all antichains. No assumption of independent source variables or monotonicity of the actual interventional response ranges is attached to these claims. The paper explicitly discusses correlated dynamical contexts in Section 4.2.
analysis: Let \(A,H\) be independent fair bits, \(E\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/4)\) independent, \(B=H\oplus E\), \(C=H\), and \(Y=A\oplus B\oplus C\). All observable source assignments have positive probability and no source causes another. Under \(\operatorname{do}(A)\), \(Y=A\oplus E\), giving \(\operatorname{MACE}(A)=1/2\). Under \(\operatorname{do}(A,B)\), \(C\) remains fair and \(Y\) is fair for every imposed assignment, giving \(\operatorname{MACE}(AB)=0\).

Adding interventions replaces mechanisms; the resulting response distributions need not contain those of the smaller intervention family. The decrease contradicts unrestricted intervention monotonicity, and the stated inversion produces a negative partial contribution \(-1/2\). Correlated contexts are permitted by the source, so independence cannot be silently added to remove the example.

For an explicit two-source decomposition, choose analyzed sources \(\{A,B\}\) while \(C\) remains background. Then \(m(A)=1/2\), \(m(B)=0\), \(m(AB)=0\) and the minimum redundancy is \(0\). Möbius reconstruction gives the joint-only atom \(m(AB)-\max\{m(A),m(B)\}=-1/2\). Every source assignment is supported, so this does not rely on unspecified off-support responses.
result: The unrestricted monotonicity and universal nonnegativity claims are false. The decomposition can still be studied with an explicit monotonicity assumption or a separately defined envelope; those changes alter its scope or meaning.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
repair: State and justify a monotonicity assumption for the intervention-effect set function, or define a monotone-envelope variant and disclose its changed scientific meaning. Neither is a replacement proof of the unrestricted original claim.
problems.impact_rationale: A fully supported correlated-source causal model falsifies the core intervention-monotonicity and nonnegative-decomposition guarantees. This directly injures the central mathematical claim and warrants Major.

problems.title: The cellular-automaton plot omits signed contributions produced by the decomposition
problems.source_location: Section 4.2, PDF p. 7; Figure 3, PDF p. 8; released notebook cells 5–6.
claim: Section 4.2, PDF p. 7, and Figure 3, PDF p. 8, compare cellular-automaton contexts. The authors' notebook, zero-based cells \(5\)–\(6\), implements simulation and plotting with a positive-only atom-selection threshold and nonnegative display limits.
analysis: Atoms never exceeding \(0.01\) are omitted by the positive-only mask, while display limits \([0,1.1]\) clip negative contributions of retained atoms. Once signed contributions are possible, those operations can hide them. The released settings of \(1000\) steps with \(0.05\) burn-in also differ from the stated \(10000\) steps with the first \(500\) removed. No new cellular-automaton simulation or negative-context frequency is claimed.
result: This is a supported local finding within the stated source/formulation scope. Its effect on the paper's aggregate experimental results remains unmeasured.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
